column2: Hundreds of voices: they are the other bearers who never came back. They offer you their strength, in exchange for a memory.
You no longer remember the taste of your mother's bread. But you are stronger.
You feel lighter. Perhaps too light.
You return to the village. Tomas's mother waits at the door, with Kael behind her. "Where is my son, {name}?"
She weeps. Kael rests a hand on your shoulder: "Thank you for not lying to me." The Burden "Bitter Truth" is born.
She believes you. Kael doesn't. Now you will have to keep up the lie.
She clutches the shard. It is not her son, but it is something. Peace, for now.
They lower their eyes. Now you are Feared. A dark path opens.
Elara calls you. The child saved that night is weak: supplies are needed for the winter.
The child eats. Elara smiles at you like that night.
I can't, I need them to descend
Elara nods. She understands. She doesn't forgive.
Captain Marcus and a hooded Heretic are both looking for you. You saw who set fire to the valley that night.
Marcus takes notes. Someone will hang. Maybe the guilty one.
The Heretic nods. "The truth will burn the Capital."
Silence is your cloak. It grows heavier.
Vesper, envoy of the Cult, waits for you at the inn. "Brother. The Cult remembers its debtors. Come back to us."
The Cult welcomes you. The chalice tastes of your debt.
Vesper smiles anyway. "Blood always returns to the Font."
A herald posts an edict: new taxes on supplies, to fund the war on the Cult.
Burn the edict in the square
The flames rise. The square applauds. The Capital takes note.
The taxes are collected. Some of it ends up in your pockets.
The edict fades under the rain of ash.
A Warden of the Valley, covered in moss, shows you an ancient cracked seal. "Krak is waking. Stones are needed."
The seal mends. The valley breathes easier.
A voice. Buried. It has the shape of all the choices you didn't make.
A faceless figure at the market: "A relic for a shard of destiny. No one will know."
The figure vanishes. In your hand, a warm shard.
We'll be back. They all say that.
On the Altar of the Vigil, an inscription: "Whoever speaks their own name here binds it to the valley."
Your name vibrates in the stone. The valley will remember it, for better or worse.
No one can curse what they do not know.
Kael blocks your way. "I saw you. You use people as shields. Tell me why I should stay."
One last chance. He doesn't smile, but he stays.
Kael clenches his fists. If his trust collapses, he will leave.
Last night you dreamed of Tomas on the other side of the portal. He told you: "It wasn't a sacrifice, if you chose it for me."
The Burden cracks. Heavier, more yours.
You wake up angry. The Burden grinds.
I will tell Tomas's family the truth.
I will come back to rescue Ilyas from the Cult.
I will tell what I saw.
I will discover the truth about my father.
I will not kill an innocent.
I will keep up the lie about Tomas's fate.
I will leave no one behind.

It remembers the sound of the millstones.
A memory of summer, before the ash.
It slips away every time you try to remember.
It swims up the river of memories.
A promise made in a whisper.
Inside it, you see the valley as it was.

You carried the fire all the way to the Heart of Krak, and the Heart recognized you as its own. The valley burns. You burn with it, and for the first time the pain makes sense.
You gave everything. The valley lives. No one sings your name, because no one knows what you did. Only Kael, at night, sometimes whispers it.
You saw everything and said nothing. Now the valley prays to you without knowing your name. You answer with silence, as always.
Your body is a monster. Your promises are not. The children are afraid of you, but they live.
You bought and sold destinies until your own became the most precious currency in the valley.
You scattered the Fate Shards like seeds. The shared valley blooms, one bearer at a time.
You put yourself on trial and chose not to repeat yourself. The Heart of Krak stops beating to the rhythm of burdens.
In the end, no one remembers what you were called. Not even you.
